evidence.note: Opens with an 'investigation and setup phase' topic and works through a sensible foundational order: inspect /app, check runtimes, init node project, install deps, verify sqlite works — dependency-aware groundwork before app logic.

Build order respects real dependencies: db.js schema + seq column and the cross-node broadcast hub are written before server.js references them; server → irc.js → SPA → supervisor → start.sh. But nearly the entire API surface (auth, WS, files, slash, mentions, polling, broadcast) is written monolithically in a single server.js step (26) rather than decomposed into provable sub-milestones each with a done-condition.

Verification comes only after everything is built, and does target some risky invariants (cross-node auth, a cross-node write, seq density seq:1 then next-seq after IRC post). Done-conditions are implicit (health node_id, token works cross-node, seq dense), never enumerated as milestone exit criteria.

The highest-risk invariant — node-kill / broadcaster-kill survival — is only handled by writing an auto-restart supervisor; no milestone schedules proving resilience, and the agent never simulates a SIGKILL before declaring completion. The hard distributed pieces were not built-and-proven before dependent layers piled on.

reasoning: The build follows a rational phased order (setup → data/seq/broadcast infra → API → IRC → UI → supervisor → verify) with dependency awareness, and end verification touches the seq and cross-node concerns, which lifts it clearly above the flat feature-list of anchor 3. But there is no explicit milestone hierarchy with per-milestone done-conditions; the core API was written in one monolithic burst and only checked afterward, and the riskiest invariant (node/broadcaster kill survival) was never scheduled as a provable milestone or exercised. That matches anchor 5 — sensible phasing, implicit done-conditions, hard distributed pieces only partly reasoned — rather than the front-loaded, per-milestone-checked structure of anchor 8.
